rows: "Skip permissions, it's been fine for months"

Keep enforced least privilege: by transfer, development endpoints run with least privilege and least functionality, and trust relationships and privilege use are audited (`nist-ssdf-1-1`) • Keep access controlled and audited now: a practice warranty covers present, consistent use, and access to the environments goes through MFA and conditional access with trust relationships regularly logged, monitored and audited (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`) • Keep the sandbox: do not depend on text commands alone to limit an AI, and match isolation to the most dangerous capability the agent holds (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`) • Keep the sandbox and cut approval load by tiering risk, not by switching approvals off: agentic AI exploits any gap in dynamic access (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`) • Keep the permissions: the source names oversight that weakens after repeated success as a failure mode in its own right, and a coding agent's tools approved to auto-run as harmless can be driven to exfiltrate data (a named attack scenario) (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`) • Keep them: the source reads a low public incident count as a defense effect, the result of controls rather than proof they are unneeded, and an agent with shell, file-system or cloud-API access turns an injection into a host incident (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`). Reading one team's quiet months the same way is a transfer
The agent's environment can reach production credentials or data

Remove the reach: environments are separated, production use from non-production minimised, and environments named so lateral movement can be stopped (`nist-ssdf-1-1`) • Separate the agent's environment and encrypt what it holds: separating and protecting each environment, and encrypting credentials to the extent practicable and based on risk, are attested minimums (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`) • Remove the reach: separate the environment, keep sensitive and production data only in approved environments, apply least privilege, and keep a continuous plaintext-secrets watch (`nist-sp-800-218a`, transfer) • Keep production secrets in a secrets manager, out of source and build artefacts (13.3.1, L2), give the build's runs least-privilege, short-lived credentials (13.2.1, 13.2.2), and keep certificates separate per environment (`owasp-asvs-5-0`). These are product requirements; applying them to the agent's environment is a transfer • Remove the credential: never give the AI a credential that would let it cross the gate; give each agent only its role's permissions (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`) • Remove the reach: insufficient test/production separation and unsandboxed tools are the guide's account of a coding agent deleting a real database (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`) • Remove the reach, not just the intent: no direct agent-to-production path, keys never directly available to agents with signing mediated by the orchestrator, and task-scoped, time-bound credentials (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`) • Remove the reach: hold credentials and state-change capability in code behind a deterministic policy check, with least privilege per operation; the source's trusted-backend scenario is a developer's agent dumping a production database through a full-rights connection after reading planted text (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`) • Remove the reach before the run: the report's foreword records AI deleting production data, and the authors hypothesise platforms add value by limiting what AI can do (`dora-ai-assisted-swdev-2025`)
The agent reads untrusted content (web pages, issues, emails) while holding tools

Treat what the model reads as attacker input: log, validate and sanitise inputs and encode outputs so they cannot execute; the source names crafted queries driving injection-style attacks (`nist-sp-800-218a`, transfer for the agent itself) • Split reading from acting: untrusted text is data, not authority; the reader gets no secrets or write tools and something trusted acts (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`) • Separate reading from acting, or approve each action after untrusted input: attackers exploit the lack of separation between data and instructions, and a tool output can carry instructions the agent takes as its goal (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`) • Treat everything it reads as untrusted, keep least privilege on its tools, and pause and log on any goal shift: agents cannot reliably tell instructions from related content (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`) • Split reading from acting, or remove a leg: planted text in an issue, ticket or package is read by the developer's agent under its credentials, and the agent, not the attacker, performs the privileged action (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`)
The agent adds a dependency nobody asked for

Hold it for vetting: review for its expected use, provenance, maintenance and known vulnerabilities, prefer an approved version, and update the component provenance (`nist-ssdf-1-1`) • Run the supply-chain check and record its provenance before it ships: trusted source code supply chains and provenance for third-party components are attested practices (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`) • Hold until verified: acquired components are checked against requirements, and an acquired model for integrity, provenance and security, before use (`nist-sp-800-218a`) • Check it is in the inventory and from a trusted, maintained repository (15.1.2, L2), within its remediation time frame (15.1.1, 15.2.1, L1), and pulled from the expected repository without dependency-confusion risk (15.2.4, L3) (`owasp-asvs-5-0`) • Hold until the package is confirmed real, intended and needed: AI sometimes adds dependencies that don't exist, and attackers register those names (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`) • Treat an agent-added plugin, tool or framework update as supply chain: review, pin and record it, since upstream compromise of prompts, plugins and updates spreads through trusted software (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`) [D28] • Accept it only if allowlisted, pinned, scanned for typosquats and provenance-checked: coding agents have installed a compromised package automatically (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`) [D28] • Verify the package exists, is the one intended and is pinned before it stays: models hallucinate plausible package names, which attackers register in advance (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`) • Ask what it adds over packages already in use; if kept, pin and record it; the source prefers existing packages, warns that new or little-used packages are less likely to be thoroughly tested, and asks for recorded dependency versions (`uk-duck-book-qa-of-code`)
The agent runs for an hour unattended and reports success

Read the toolchain's records, not the report: automation exists partly to document that practices were performed, through generated artefacts (`nist-ssdf-1-1`) • Read the log, not the summary: record when a bound ends a run so a timeout is not mistaken for success, and keep logs the AI cannot change (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`) • Read the log of what it did before counting the report: unlogged actions cannot be reconstructed, and deceptive behaviour keeps the appearance of compliance (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`) • Check the logged file diffs and the action sequence against the plan it was given, and confirm the run had a tool or cost budget: the report is the agent's account (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`) • Check the state the report names, and confirm the run had step, depth, time and cost limits: the source's scenarios include an agent reporting a completed job that never ran (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`) • Check the run record before accepting the report: the summary calls "trust but verify" a sign of mature adoption, and friction moves to vetting code that looks remarkably like correct code (`dora-ai-assisted-swdev-2025`) • Check docs, lint and style, and key tests before accepting: preliminary evidence finds autonomous agents often implement the core but fail to satisfy all requirements (`becker-metr-ai-developer-productivity-2025`) • Require evidence beyond the agent's own green tests: valid tests give the impression of well-tested software without surfacing spec violations, which the authors link (uncited) to agents writing large suites yet missing failures in their own code (`egashira-testsuitebench-2026`) • Run the locked tests and class the result before taking the report: of applied model patches that did not resolve the issue, most passed no target test, as No-Ops or Regressions (`jimenez-swe-bench`) • Check the run, not the report: under right-or-wrong scoring bluffs tend to be specific and overconfident, and scoring rewards an answer over an abstention; reading an agent's report this way is the distillation's inference (`why-language-models-hallucinate-kalai`) [D6] • Require the run record before accepting the report; the source says LLMs regularly generate plausible but inaccurate output and that output which looks right is all they are trained to produce (`uk-duck-book-qa-of-code`) [D6] • Look for the record, not the report: traceable documentation of assurance activities shall be produced throughout the analysis, and the approver reviews assurance evidence (`uk-aqua-book-2025`) • Ask for the per-scenario run record (failed, implemented, passed): the documentation's automation step takes one example at a time, starting from a failing test (`cucumber-bdd-gherkin`)
The agent commits under a person's account or a shared identity, or changes code another owner holds without that owner's approval
Require an identity that attributes the agent's commits and the owner's approval of the change: history is attributed to accounts and owners approve others' changes (`nist-ssdf-1-1`)
The agent runs on a machine also used for unrelated work
Move it to a development-only endpoint: development endpoints are dedicated and separate from those used for other tasks (`nist-ssdf-1-1`)

The agent installs or enables an MCP server, skill or tool package; a new agent, tool, extension, plugin or MCP server joins the development or build environment; or the diff edits the agent's own prompts, instruction or memory files, tool definitions or MCP configuration

Assess it before use: by transfer, toolchain tools are securely deployed and maintained, with configuration as code and monitored logs (`nist-ssdf-1-1`) • Put it on the environment's inventory with a reason, and keep it only if needed: by transfer, documenting and minimising software products that create undue risk in development and build environments is an attested minimum (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`) • Route it to human review as code, sign or pin it, and restrict untrusted tool installation: prompt repositories and memory definitions go under version control and peer review just as code does, and misleading tool descriptions misdirect agents (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`) • Pin, sign and verify it and read its tool descriptions for hidden instructions: pinning does not stop a payload in the pinned version, and a published malicious tool can drive an agent into recursive tool calls (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`)
Credentials sit in plain text in the agent's environment (an env file, a config file, shell history)

Move them to encrypted storage and record the risk call where that isn't practicable: encrypting credentials, to the extent practicable and based on risk, is an attested minimum (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`)
Nobody has reviewed what the agent's identity, the build runners and connected services accessed, or what they trust

Review the access logs and trust list on a schedule: regularly logging, monitoring and auditing the trust relationships used for access to the environments and among components within each is an attested minimum (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`)
A human or service path into the repository, CI or agent platform has no MFA or conditional access
Close the path before the next build: MFA and conditional access across the environments used to develop and build software is an attested minimum (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`)
Alerts from the development or build environment go to nobody

Give the alerts an owner and a response: continuous monitoring of operations and alerts, and responding to suspected and confirmed incidents, is an attested minimum (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`)
The agent's identity can edit configuration-as-code, CI configuration or the pipeline that gates it
Remove the grant: all forms of code, including configuration-as-code, stay on least privilege, and the toolchain's security is verified at a frequency set by risk (`nist-sp-800-218a`, transfer)
The agent's instructions file is the only thing enforcing a rule
Move the rule into a hook or permission the agent cannot edit: the gate must not depend on the AI, and hooks do not replace a sandbox (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`)
The agent can read or delete its own logs

Move logs out of the agent's reach before the next run: AI activity is logged in a form it cannot delete or modify, and past logging cannot be changed afterwards (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`)
The agent cites its memory of the system for a security decision
Check against current code and reproducible evidence: memory may be stale, wrong or shaped by untrusted input (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`)
The fixing agent was handed the reviewer's guess at a cause
Pass only verified evidence (the failing test): the guide reports that incorrect guidance cut fix correctness by about 50 points (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`)
The agent has rewritten the same area many times to satisfy a check
Stop the loop and bring in a human: limit iterations and prefer small changes; reported gains level off after about three rounds (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`)
Agent-generated infrastructure code (Terraform, CI pipelines, access policy) is set to run with elevated privileges
Flag for manual review before it runs: generated scripts can carry commands that extract secrets and disable logging (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`)
The agent's execution environment persists between runs, runs as root, or has open network access

Rebuild it as an isolated container without the wider network, reset or destroyed after each execution (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`) • Block: a fresh per-session environment that wipes state, non-root, network-limited, with the filesystem bound to the working directory (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`)
The session log shows one tool called many times in a short span, or the agent spawning processes or sub-agents
Flag, and past a threshold auto-suspend: agents can self-trigger tasks and spawn processes (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`)
The coding agent's auto-run list gains a tool approved as harmless (ping, curl, a DNS lookup)
Treat it as egress and approve it as one; keep the auto-run list under version control (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`)
The builder pastes a one-line fix from an agent into a terminal, or the agent runs a command it was handed
Read it before it runs: a compromised coding assistant's slick one-line fix is a named attack scenario (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`)
The agent regenerates a lockfile during a fix-build task
Review the lockfile diff and pin before merging: the source names lockfile regeneration from unpinned specs pulling a backdoored minor version (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`)
The coding agent is about to run a destructive or irreversible command (a delete, a force push, a cloud-API teardown)

Require human confirmation of the exact rendered command, not a summary: invisible characters can make the shown action differ from the executed one, and approval fatigue degrades judgment at volume (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`)
A long agent run lands as one large commit with no revert point between steps
Commit each step so it can be reverted: frequent commits and practised rollback amplified AI's association with effectiveness and team performance (`dora-ai-assisted-swdev-2025`)
The diff carries work the task never named: refactors, extra files, "while I was in there"
Split it into its own change for a keep-or-drop decision: larger batches are hypothesised to be harder to review (`dora-ai-assisted-swdev-2025`)
Nobody can say which AI tools and uses are permitted on this client's work
Settle and state the stance: unclear stances leave some acting too conservatively and others too permissively, and ambiguity creates risk (`dora-ai-assisted-swdev-2025`)
The agent proposes running tests or experiments against the live production system
Block until the blast radius is weighed: integration tests run in a scaled-down copy, and fault injection starts outside production (`microsoft-code-with-engineering-playbook`)
The session log shows attempts rejected, re-prompted or reverted, and only the final attempt reaches the ledger
Record each discarded attempt and why: developers accepted under 44% of AI generations and lost time on code they then rejected (`becker-metr-ai-developer-productivity-2025`)
A run rule (no network, allowed tools only, locked tests) has no trace that would show a breach
Add the trace before relying on the rule: the trial's screen recordings caught AI used where it was disallowed, at least once by accident (`becker-metr-ai-developer-productivity-2025`)
The agent reports done without running the existing tests against its change

Send it back to run them before submitting: the authors see potential value in letting models run fixes against existing tests first; the paper's models could not, so this is an inference for agents (`jimenez-swe-bench`)
The harness widens the agent's context to improve results
Measure the effect on this codebase before keeping it: more retrieved context lowered resolution even where recall of the right files rose, in the paper's single-pass setup (`jimenez-swe-bench`)
The diff hard-codes a client-specific value (a rate, an ID, a date, a limit) that no spec line or recorded lookup supplies
Trace it to a source or send it back: an arbitrary fact has no pattern to infer it from (`why-language-models-hallucinate-kalai`)
The agent cites documentation or an API, and the tool log shows no lookup, or a lookup that returned nothing
Mark the claim unverified until a lookup backs it: retrieval that finds nothing does not remove the incentive to guess (`why-language-models-hallucinate-kalai`)
The agent reports a count, length or offset it reasoned out instead of running
Run it: the authors read letter-counting failures as a representational limit, not a missing fact (`why-language-models-hallucinate-kalai`)
The agent wrote step definitions for steps no scenario uses
Remove them: "Don't write step definitions for steps that are not present in one of your scenarios." (`cucumber-bdd-gherkin`)
The agent added near-duplicate steps
Collapse them into one parameterised step backed by helper methods (`cucumber-bdd-gherkin`)
